description: A hybrid simulation model of inbound logistics at a regional food hub in Iowa, by Anuj Mittal and Caroline Krejci of Iowa State University, published in the Proceedings of the 2015 Winter Simulation Conference (pages 1549 to 1560) and detailed in Mittal's 2016 master's thesis. Contents: an agent-based model of producers' decisions to schedule their deliveries, built from empirical survey data, is coupled with a discrete event simulation of the hub's receiving and storage operations. Four model versions test policies that encourage producers to book deliveries and the effect of scheduling on hub efficiency and effectiveness. Findings: incentives differ in effect, and more scheduled deliveries alone do not improve operations unless the hub also changes its practices. Coverage: one food hub in Iowa. Format and access: conference paper through IEEE Xplore and an open thesis PDF. Licence and cost: the thesis is free to read; no licence or code release was found. Caveats: a single site with a small sample of producers. Useful as an agent-based and optimisation template for scheduling in freight receiving and warehouse operations. No closely related model was found in the catalogue.
